scope: Functional collector verification with original controlled workload callbacks and complete fixture-start-through-owner-reap boundary. Configuration-time JavaScript enrollment and original test-event dispatch observation; optional native diagnostics. Instrumentation cost included.
checks: All six original controlled families at one and four workers on both frameworks.
All four-worker cells observed overlapping original test dispatch intervals.
All 60 intentional failures retained verified original error, callsite, code frame and fixture snapshot.
Kernel unique process and parent identities join original JavaScript launches to native owner records.
Coherent executable-path observations allow only the pinned wrapper-to-browser image change with ordered observations and increasing global version.
All captures exited normally without watchdog timeout, cleanup signals or remaining observed processes.
Source, JavaScript dependencies, pinned executables and GN-declared native runtime dependencies unchanged before and after the batch.
priorAttemptsRetained: Configuration and launch observation failures retained separately.
Exact version and one-step version assumptions rejected valid wrapper exec handoffs; macOS uses a shared global fork/exec version counter.
limitations: Controlled families only; current application collector integration remains open.
Test dispatch intervals include fixtures and hooks; they are not callback-only timing.
Kernel queries before parent-observed exit do not prove a process was non-zombie.
Sampled RSS is non-atomic and is neither a true peak nor an enforced limit.
Original root wait4 CPU is recorded once; independent complete descendant accounting and final resource adapter admission remain open.
The native runtime manifest hashes GN-declared runtime dependencies; it is not an observed file-access inventory.
One functional batch, with a development browser profile; no speed or final performance claim.
Native Linux remains unverified by user direction.
